2. These two appeals are filed against the judgment and award passed in MVC No.380/2020 dated 04.08.2023 by NC: 2025:KHC-K:7101 C/W MFA.CROB No. 200079 of 2025 HC-KAR the Prl.
District and Sessions Judge and M.A.C.T at Raichur (for short 'the Tribunal').

sentences.text: 3. Injured/claimant - Ramesh son of Hudadayya, aged 35 years, stone maker, met with an accident on 16.04.2019 and filed a claim claiming compensation of Rs.53,00,000/-.
The Tribunal granted Rs.10,01,069/- with interest at the rate of 6% from the date of petition and directed respondent No.2 to deposit the amount within the three months.
4. Aggrieved by the said order, the Insurance company preferred MFA No.200068/2024 and the claimants preferred MFA Crob. No.200079/2025.

Ramesh vs Amarappa Jadedhar on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121365172/
3

5. Insurance company mainly contended that, the Tribunal granted higher compensation on loss of future earnings and needs to be modified and the compensation granted for transportation expenses are higher and compensation under other conventional heads needs to be reduced.
6.

In the cross-objections filed by the claimants, he contended that, he was earning Rs.30,000 per month as a stone worker, but no amount was granted under the head loss of NC: 2025:KHC-K:7101 C/W MFA.CROB No. 200079 of 2025 HC-KAR earning during laid up period and meager amounts are granted under other heads.
Therefore, requested for enhancement of compensation.
7. The counsel for the appellant i.e., Insurance Company further contended that, the father's name of claimant was shown as Hudadayya in the petition.
But in the FIR and complaint, his father's name was shown as Ramesh son of Gudadappa.
But the said aspect was not raised in the petition or before the Tribunal.
The identity of the claimant was not disputed before the Tribunal at the earliest point of time.
Therefore, now it cannot be considered.
8. Though it is stated that appellant was earning Rs.30,000/- per month, he has not filed any income proof.

As he met with an accident on 16.04.2019, as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, his notional income is taken as Rs.13,250/- per month and this Court finds no reason to interfere with the said order.
9. PW2 examined the appellant and assessed the disability as 35%.
The Tribunal has taken the disability as 30%.

Petitioner sustained fracture shaft of left tibia and fibula in distal NC:
2025:KHC-K:7101 C/W MFA.CROB No. 200079 of 2025 HC-KAR one third and fracture of 1st, 2nd,
3rd, 4th and 5th meta tasrsals of left foot.
It is further observed that there is swelling and infection of the left leg, multiple discharge of sinus in left leg and damage over left leg.
Internal and external rotation of hip is painful.
He cannot sit and squat.
He cannot walk for long distances and climb the stairs.
He cannot lift heavy weight and accordingly, the disability was assessed as 35% to the whole body.
Hence, considering the occupation of the appellant as stone worker, the Tribunal has rightly taken the disability as 30% and this Court finds no reasons interfere with the said disability.
10. In the disability certificate, the estimated cost of the future medical expenses was shown as 30,000/-.
The Tribunal granted Rs.14,869/- towards medical expenses and Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses and this court finds no reasons to interfere with the said amounts.
11. He was hospitalized for 40 days.
The amounts granted by the tribunal under other heads are just and proper and it needs no interference.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7101 C/W MFA.CROB No. 200079 of 2025 HC-KAR 12.
The Tribunal has rightly considered all the aspects and granted Rs.10,01,069/- and this Court finds no reason to interfere with the said order.

13. In the result, the following order is passed:
